newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Investments exploring sales in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investments exploring sales in Japan.

text.p: Mutual fund giant Fidelity Investments said on Thursday it is exploring the potential for sales of mutual funds and brokerage services to individuals and institutions in Japan.
The company is requesting Japan Ministry of Finance approval to open a representative office of Fidelity Brokerage Services Inc in Tokyo, Fidelity said.

Arthur Jesson, who currently heads Fidelity's client services, trading and systems operation in Asia, has been promoted to senior vice president of Fidelity Brokerage Services Japan, said Fidelity, a unit of FMR Corp.
Jesson becomes the manager of the representative office pending the approval from the Japanese Ministry of Finance.

Fidelity Investments opened its first Asian office in Japan in 1969 and now manages more than US$10 billion in Japanese investments for individuals and corporations worldwide, the company said. Fidelity's investment office in Tokyo currently has a staff of more than 60 employees, the company said.
